title: Elastic pool operator cheatsheet & wireframe notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an operator-focused cheat sheet and wireframe writeup for the "elastic pool" view in the Dedicated Capacity console. Target audience: SREs, platform operators, on-call engineers, and solutions engineers who manage multi-tenant GPU pools, autoscale rules, reservation overrides, and burst events. The doc purpose is tactical: capture wireframe decisions, failure-mode flows, quick-runbooks, and a prioritized backlog of UX polish items that unblock on-call tasks.

Why a separate operator view?
- Operators need dense telemetry and action affordances (drain, force-evict, soft-drain, manual-scale) without the conversational/marketing chrome users see.
- Fast triage beats pretty dashboards when customers are impacted.
- Allowing low-friction overrides (temporary burst, emergency routing, forced fallbacks) reduces ticket MTTR.

Personas and scenarios (short):
- Pool Operator (SRE): needs to see pool-level health, queue depth, average token p99 latency, and quick actions to isolate noisy tenants. Typical flow: detect latency spike -> identify tenant(s) -> soft-drain -> migrate or bump reserved capacity.
- Capacity Planner (platform): reviews historical growth, reservation conflicts, and can schedule capacity bumps/bursts. Needs timeline and predicted SLO breaches.
- Solutions Eng (customer-facing): runs manual canary for a customer's model rollout into a reserved pool. Needs rollout controls and visibility into canary traffic.

Wireframe components (operator-first):
- Top header (compact): pool name, pool id, region, tier, health pill (green/amber/red) + last updated timestamp. Small action menu: Edit config / Snapshot config / Export logs.
- Left rail (condensed): Pools list (search, filter by region/tier/label) + collapsed 'Quick actions' (global soft-drain, global emergency-burst).
- Main canvas split (two columns):
  Column A (wide):
  - Live summary card: p50/p95/p99 latencies, queued requests, tokens/sec, serving throughput (tokens/s), active GPUs, memory usage %. Each metric has a tiny sparkline (1h/24h toggle).
  - Top callers table (compact): tenant id, active requests, avg latency, top models, option to open 'tenant drill' drawer.
  - Alert timeline: chronological list of recent autoscale events, manual bursts, forced fallbacks, with a quick filter for 'acknowledged/unacknowledged'.

  Column B (narrow):
  - Action deck (stacked cards): Manual scale slider (live preview of expected throughput + cost delta), Soft-drain toggle with policy dropdown (grace period), Reservation quick-create form (small), Burst quick-start buttons (1m/5m/15m) with pre-checks.
  - Recent executions: list of last 10 operator-initiated actions with undo where applicable.

- Tenant drill (right drawer): tenant metadata, recent requests (sample ids), tail logs link, option to 'evict' or 'isolate to secondary pool'. Drawer also surfaces ticket links and last contact note.

Operator flows and micro-interactions:
1) Soft-drain a noisy tenant: open tenant drill -> click soft-drain -> choose drain window (default 5m) and migration target (auto-select compatible pool). Confirmation modal shows impact estimate (requests affected, tokens dropped, estimated latency change). Acceptance: operator can complete flow in <= 3 clicks.

2) Emergency burst: from Pool header -> Burst -> choose burst size (small/medium/large) or custom GPUs -> safety checks run (budget cap, GPU availability) -> preview cost + fallback policy -> Start (non-blocking). UI shows 'burst countdown' and toast with link to burst progress panel. Acceptance: burst start latency < 5s, clear rollback button.

3) Canary rollout into pool: action deck -> Start canary -> select % traffic (1/5/10) and model version -> choose target slice (playback vs live) -> automated traffic replay option for deterministic tests -> observe canary metrics panel. Acceptance: canary created and visible in timeline with expected sample size.

Accessibility and keyboard shortcuts:
- Dense operator screens must support keyboard-first operations: / to focus global search, G then P opens pool list, D opens tenant drawer for selected row, B opens burst dialog.
- Color contrast: no critical status encoded by color only; badges have icons and text.

Edge cases and failure modes (UX notes):
- If autoscale controller is offline: show an obvious banner and grey out manual-scale slider; provide a single-click 'override' with heavier confirmation.
- If a burst can't be fulfilled (no spare GPUs): clearly explain whether failure is due to region shortage, quota, or budget. Provide a suggested remediation (e.g., fallback to compatible region or propose preemption).
- During long operations (migrations, large canary deployments): surface progress + a compact timeline entry and allow ops to annotate with ticket ids.

Backlog (prioritized):
- INF-901: Add 'operator-mode' compact header with last action undo (P0). Criteria: undo available for 2 minutes for manual scale and soft-drain.
- INF-902: Implement burst pre-check panel with simulated cost and compatibility checks (P0).
- INF-918: Tenant drill: quick log sample + ability to open live stream (P1).
- INF-937: Keyboard shortcut wiring + onboarding tooltip (P1).
- INF-989: Historic 'what-if' capacity simulator baked into pool page (P2).
- INF-1001: Add audit trail export CSV for last 30 days of operator actions (P2).

Acceptance criteria for snippet features:
- Manual-scale slider: must show realistic throughput delta and cost estimate within 10% of backend calculation.
- Soft-drain: migration target suggestions must only include pools with compatible GPU types and sufficient headroom.
- Burst button: protected by per-org budget cap; starting a burst logs an event and creates a trace id.

Mock text for UI copy (concise):
- Soft-drain CTA: "Soft-drain tenant — allow running tasks to finish, prevent new assignments (5m default)"
- Burst preview header: "Burst preview — estimated +$X/hr, will provision 2x T4-equivalents"
- Canary start button: "Start canary (1% traffic)"

Operational runbook snippets (copy-paste for pager duty runbook):
1) Detecting pool degradation:
  - Check live summary card for p99 spikes and queued requests > 25% of active capacity.
  - Open top callers to find tenant(s) causing queue.
  - If single tenant: soft-drain and escalate to solutions eng.
  - If multi-tenant: consider manual-scale or emergency burst.
2) Starting emergency burst:
  - Confirm budget cap in console -> open burst panel -> run pre-check -> start -> message on-call channel with burst trace id.
  - Monitor 'burst progress' tile for provisioning errors; if fails, start fallback policy (route to lower-cost model variant).

Data and telemetry we need from backend (for implementation notes):
- Live aggregated metrics: tokens/sec, active_gpus, cuda_mem_pct, kv_cache_hit_rate, average_batch_size, queued_reqs.
- Per-tenant recent request samples + model_version tags.
- Autoscaler status object (online/offline, last_tick, last_error).
- Reservation metadata (owner, schedule, capacity delta, linked tickets).

Design variants considered (why we chose current layout):
- Variant A: full-width timeline-first layout — rejected because too slow for quick action.
- Variant B: operator-only compact dashboard — good for on-call but blocks context for planners. Chosen hybrid: dense metrics + focused action deck.

Prototype notes and next steps:
- Create Figma prototype screens: pool list, pool detail (two-column), tenant drawer, burst flow, canary flow. Aim for clickable demo for SREs by 2025-02-20.
- Frontend tasks: build compact metrics components with server-sent events for real-time updates.
- Backend tasks: expose pre-check api for bursts and a lightweight 'simulate-scale' endpoint.

Open questions for PM/Infra:
- Who owns budget enforcement for bursts? (org-level or pool-level?)
- What retention window should operator audit export use by default? 30 days or 90 days?

Notes to reviewer:
- This intentionally includes operator-first interactions that will not be in the customer-facing pool page. We should discuss toggling an 'operator-mode' flag so that the same route can be rendered with or without the action deck.

Signoff: Ava Martinez (PM, Platform Engineering). Last pass: 2025-02-05.
